chapter: The war years: Barnet, Hot Lips Page, Newton and Kirby
title: Accompanying Gladys Lundy in tails
summary: He played for Gladys Lundy, a masculine-dressed singer of spicy special material who later turned religious.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: We are now going to leave Asbury Park and go to New York, Tondelayo's(?) and Erroll Garner.

Well, when I heard him play, and the more I listened to him, the more I stayed, and I forgot about the axe...the more interested I became in playing the axe/acts(?), and not trying to outplay him, because...
But weren't you playing, accompanying somebody?
Yeah. I was playing with Gladys Lundy(?).
Didn't Gladys do a sort of masculine thing or something?
Yeah, she worked masculine, and she did special material.
Special material could mean something a bit funny, huh.

Well... Yeah, she would... You had to know... If you worked for her... I worked for her first... But at one time earlier, in my earlier days... I worked for her before... Oh, Dave Martin, the late Dave Martin; Eddie Heywood worked for her.

And so I had a nice thing going, working for her, working for the (?), too. She did special material, like "The Boys Up At Yale," very spicy sort of material. Something like "The swimming of the organ and the coming of the bride", things like... [LAUGHS]
But by this time... She was a good bit older than you, wasn't she.
Oh, I would say she was a bit more experienced. She had been around. It's funny, during her later years, her final years, she became religious.
Oh yeah. After doing all that, you know,
working in tails and pants... She was way ahead of her time, believe me. Today she'd be a queen, you know! I mean, the ERA would really be all right with her. But she changed...
